Primary objectives of the trial are (i) the evaluation of the safety of HOLOGENE 7 and the CLINICAL STUDY PROTOCOL Study design The study is a phase I/II multicentric, prospective, open label, uncontrolled, interventional, pilot clinical trial. It will be conducted in centers of excellence in Europe, with strong experience on the treatment of RDEB patients. The phase I/II study design is proposed to ensure fast access for patients to a new drug expected to be safe and effective, as no alternative drugs are currently available for a permanent long-lasting treatment of RDEB (Figure 29). Details of the clinical study design will not be discussed as they are still confidential. Figure 29. Outline of Hologene 7 clinical study. Created with Biorender.com. Primary objectives of the trial are (i) the evaluation of the safety of HOLOGENE 7 and the procedures associated with its administration (infections, lack of engraftment, transplant rejection, immunoreactions), (ii) evaluation of the patient’s safety measured by occurrence of adverse events, treatment-emergent adverse events, adverse events of special interest, and serious adverse events at any time during the study. As secondary objective, HOLOGENE 7 efficacy (defined as clinical and functional epidermal restoration) will be evaluated. At least twelve patients (pediatric and adult) affected by RDEB will be progressively enrolled, on an expected 12-months recruitment period. The patient enrolment will be by invitation and participation is voluntary. The Principal Investigator (PI) will identify and pre-screen suitable patients considering the clinical history of RDEB patients examined in the center. Patients will be screened according to Inclusion and Exclusion criteria (confidential; not reported) and included in the trial if all inclusion and none of the exclusion criteria are met, as well as considering Investigator's scientific and clinical experience. PRX-110, or AIR DNase, is our plant cell recombinant form of human deoxyribonuclease I (DNase I) that we are developing for the treatment of CF to be administered by inhalation.   PRX-110, or AIR DNase, is our plant cell recombinant form of human deoxyribonuclease I (DNase I) that we are developing for the treatment of CF to be administered by inhalation. DNase I cleaves extracellular DNA and thins the thick mucus that accumulates in the lungs of CF patients. Currently, Pulmozyme^{®} is the only DNase I commercially available, with annual sales of approximately CHF 652 million (approximately $652 million) in sales for 2015, an increase of 10%, according to public reports by F. Hoffman-La Roche Ltd.   In vitro studies with PRX-110 demonstrated improved enzyme kinetics, significantly reduced sensitivity to inhibition by actin and improved ex vivo efficacy when compared to Pulmozyme. Preclinical studies of PRX-110 administered by inhalation showed substantial enzymatic activity in lungs.   AIR DNase has an actin inhibition resistance that is designed to improve lung function and lower the incidence of recurrent infections by enhancing the enzyme’s efficacy in patients’ sputa.   Actin, a potent inhibitor of DNase, is found in high concentration in CF patients’ sputum. As demonstrated in Figure 1, the activity of AIR DNase remains almost with no change in the relevant actin concentration found in CF patients while Pulmozyme is degraded significantly.     | 11 |       Figure 1. Actin and DNase concentrations in human sputum tested in in vitro assays   Image   |   In addition, the product candidate has demonstrated improved disease parameters in human models sputum testing when compared to the currently marketed product. In particular, AIR DNase has demonstrated a reduction in mucus viscosity in human sputum sample when compared to the currently marketed product.
